title: Greywater Bay Rising Anew
premise: Estate lawyer August Underhill is summoned to Greywater Bay to probate the will of drowned fisherman Elias Vann — a will dated three days after Elias's death, witnessed by two people who swear they never met him. As August untangles the impossible document, a confession letter arrives postmarked the day after the funeral, naming August's own late mother among those who buried a drowning thirty years ago that was no accident. Following alibis woven across three decades, August discovers the will is a dead man's trap for his killers and that their mother helped stage the original 'accident' to survive. In the end, August chooses inheritance over innocence: they burn the confession, let the will stand, and watch the guilty inherit a town that will never stop remembering.
about_author: Ansel Blackwood is the pen name of a former maritime claims adjuster who spent fifteen years reading other people's accounts of how things went wrong at sea. They write from a houseboat on an unnamed estuary, where the fog does most of the editing.

chapters.title: The Will That Wasn't Written
chapters.summary: August Underhill arrives in fog-bound Greywater Bay to read the will of Elias Vann, drowned a week prior. The document is dated after his death and signed by witnesses who deny knowing him. August's POV; the beat is professional unease curdling into fascination as the first impossibility refuses explanation.

chapters.title: Postmarked Yesterday
chapters.summary: A letter arrives confessing to murder, postmarked the day after the funeral, addressed to August by name. Inside: details of a drowning thirty years ago that matches a case file August once closed. August's POV; the emotional beat is the floor dropping out — this letter knows things only a killer or a ghost should know.

chapters.title: Witnesses to Nothing
chapters.summary: August interviews the two witnesses: Vann's estranged daughter Maren and the town's aging harbormaster, both with airtight alibis for the night of the death — and both lying about something smaller. Alternating POV between August and Maren; the beat is the slow realization that everyone in Greywater Bay rehearses their answers.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Tide Charts
chapters.summary: Digging into archives, August reconstructs the 1994 drowning of a young deckhand ruled accidental, finding Vann's name in the crew manifest. Their mother's handwriting appears on a deposition page. August's POV; the beat is dread turning personal — the past isn't just nearby, it's in the family.

chapters.title: What Mother Kept
chapters.summary: August searches their late mother's effects and finds a Greywater Bay address book, a pawn ticket, and half-burned photographs. A neighbor recalls their mother visiting the bay every summer without explanation. August's POV; the beat is grief complicated by betrayal — love and suspicion sharing one body.

chapters.title: The Alibi Loom
chapters.summary: Maren's chapter: she remembers her father teaching her to weave stories as a child, drilling alibis like knots. She realizes the will's impossible date was deliberate — Elias built it to force an investigation. The beat is reluctant alliance; she gives August the first true thread.

chapters.title: Three Funerals, One Bay
chapters.summary: August maps three deaths across thirty years — the deckhand, a retired constable, now Vann — each following someone's attempt to speak. The surviving conspirators begin circling August, offering money, then threats. August's POV; rising tension as the mystery becomes a countdown.

chapters.title: Low Water
chapters.summary: Lured to the tidal flats at night, August confronts the last living conspirator, who admits the 1994 killing but insists August's mother orchestrated the cover-up to save them all — including herself. August's POV; the climax begins as survival and guilt become indistinguishable.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: At the formal will reading, August reveals the trap: Elias's postdated will activates only if his death is proven murder, disinheriting the killers and endowing the deckhand's forgotten family. The room detonates. August's POV; the beat is cold triumph shadowed by what revealing it costs.

chapters.title: Greywater, Rising
chapters.summary: August burns the confession letter at the tideline, choosing mercy for the dead over justice for the living, and signs the estate closed. Maren watches from the seawall; neither speaks. Final alternating POV; the resolution lands on inheritance as burden — the bay keeps its memory, and so do they.
